paper.title: CANDI: Curated Test-Time Adaptation for Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection Under Distribution Shift
paper.venue: AAAI 2026 (Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, vol. 40, no. 17, pp. 15018--15026)

compatibility.reason: CANDI is a test-time adaptation framework for unsupervised multivariate time-series anomaly detection under distribution shift; the official repository trains a reconstruction detector on normal data and evaluates anomaly detection with AUROC/AUPRC on multivariate benchmarks (SWaT, 51 variables; SMD, 38 variables). Only multivariate datasets are exercised, so dataset_types is limited to MTS; univariate (UTS) operation is not demonstrated by the released scripts.
compatibility.compute_device_evidence: trainer.py::prepare_inputs moves every input tensor to the current GPU via 'return inputs.cuda()' unconditionally, and utils/misc.py::set_seeds calls torch.cuda.manual_seed/torch.cuda.manual_seed_all and sets cudnn.deterministic; config.py sets NUM_GPUS=4 and VISIBLE_DEVICES=0. No CPU fallback path is present in the training/prediction entrypoint (main.py).

uncertainty: The arXiv identifier 2604.01845 is a future-dated (2026) identifier; the paper metadata was resolved from the arXiv abstract page and cross-checked against the repository's BibTeX entry, which agree on title, author list and venue.
The repository README mentions an additional TSB-AD evaluation under the 'TSB-AD/' directory for 200 multivariate datasets; that path is an auxiliary benchmark harness and was not inspected.
